name: WizardDialog
intent: Multi-step authoring modal: a Stepper rail, one lazily mounted step at a time, and a Next that is never disabled but reveals the current step's errors rather than advancing past them.
when: Authoring a record whose fields do not fit one screen
A create flow with a genuine review step before commit
A staged operation where a later step derives from an earlier one — plan, then apply
whenNot: The form fits one screen -> use FormDialog
The steps are a progress indicator rather than a form -> use Stepper directly
A long onboarding flow that owns the whole viewport -> use a page template, not a dialog

chooseOver.because: WizardDialog owns step position, the per-step attempted flag and its clearing on every move, the Step N of M counter, and which of Back/Next/submit is showing — the chrome three shipped wizards had each copied.
Use FormDialog when the fields fit one screen; a wizard's cost is only worth paying when they do not.

title.note: Fixed across steps; the rail communicates position.

steps.note: Each step declares its label, its own `valid`, and its content. Content may be a function of {attempted}.

submitLabel.note: Shown in place of Next on the last step.

onSubmit.note: Runs on the last step when its `valid` holds.

onReset.note: Clears the caller's field state. Runs on close AND after a successful submit; step position resets too.

width.note: Max width in px. Defaults to 720.

dataContract.rowIdentity: Steps are identified by their `label`, which must therefore be unique within one wizard.

steps[].nextLabel.description: Per-step override of the Next button

states.default: Opens on step 1; Back is absent rather than disabled.
states.refused: Next pressed on a step whose `valid` is false: position holds and the step's content re-renders with attempted true.
states.advanced: Position moves and `attempted` clears, so an error already moved past does not follow the user.
states.last: Next is replaced by the submit button; the same validity gate applies.
states.reopened: Step position and `attempted` both reset, so the next open starts at step 1.

evaluationCriteria: Only the current step is mounted.
Moving between steps clears the attempted flag.
Re-opening returns to step 1 with cleared fields.

lineage.authoredBy: Extracted from the three copied wizard chromes found in the missing-widgets template review (2026-08-25)

extracted: horizontal Stepper rail across the step labels
never-disable Next with a per-step attempted flag
attempted cleared on every step change
Step N of M footer counter
Back absent on the first step, submit replacing Next on the last

lineage.supersedes: The private WizardSteps chrome in object-type-wizard.tsx, wc3-action-type-wizard.tsx and wc3-product-install-dialog.tsx
notes: wc3-product-install-dialog.tsx:280 carried the comment 'Wizard chrome (copied from object-type-wizard.tsx / wc3-action-type-wizard.tsx)' — this widget is what that comment was asking for.
Lazy step mounting keeps a derived Review step free until it is reached.

usage: Use WizardDialog when you need to display content that temporarily overlays the main interface. This component is useful for focused interactions, confirmations, or supplementary information.
WizardDialog should be used sparingly as overlays interrupt the user's workflow. Reserve this component for important interactions that require user attention or action before continuing.

props.name: title
props.description: Dialog heading. Stays fixed across steps; the Stepper communicates position.

anatomy.description: WizardDialog is composed of the following parts:

parts.name: WizardDialogTrigger
parts.description: Element that opens the dialog when activated.

parts.name: WizardDialogContent
parts.description: Container for the dialog content and overlay.

parts.name: WizardDialogHeader
parts.description: Header section containing title and description.

bestPractices.title: Focus management
bestPractices.description: Trap focus within the dialog and return focus when closed.

bestPractices.title: Don't nest dialogs
bestPractices.description: Avoid opening dialogs from within dialogs, use sequential flow instead.

bestPractices.title: Provide clear exit
bestPractices.description: Always include a visible close button and support Escape key.

bestPractices.title: Don't trap users
bestPractices.description: Never make dialogs impossible to close or require specific actions to dismiss.
bestPractices.example: // No close button or escape handling

bestPractices.title: Keep content focused
bestPractices.description: Limit dialog content to a single task or decision.

bestPractices.title: Don't overload dialogs
bestPractices.description: Avoid putting complex forms or multiple tasks in a single dialog.
